name: Italian nationalism
summary: Italian nationalism holds that Italians form one nation whose unity, Latin and Roman heritage and standing among nations should be the supreme political aim. In its classic early-twentieth-century form, led by Enrico Corradini and Alfredo Rocco, it demanded irredentist and colonial expansion, military discipline, an elitist and anti-parliamentary state, and a corporatist organisation of classes under the nation, treating Italy as a 'proletarian nation' against plutocratic powers.
scope: The profile represents the Italian Nationalist Association (1910-1923) strand of Corradini, Rocco and L'Idea Nazionale: authoritarian, imperialist, corporatist, monarchist and anti-socialist nationalism. It is not the earlier Risorgimento nationalism of Mazzini and Cavour (republican or liberal, anti-clerical, democratic), nor post-1945 parties such as the MSI, Lega or Brothers of Italy; where the strands differ, the notes say so. Many statements on modern issues are inferred, so many answers are low confidence.

keyFigures.name: Enrico Corradini
keyFigures.role: Founder and leader of the Italian Nationalist Association; coined 'proletarian nation'.

keyFigures.name: Alfredo Rocco
keyFigures.role: Jurist who developed the ANI's corporate state theory from 1913-14.

keyFigures.name: Giuseppe Mazzini
keyFigures.role: Founder of Young Italy and central figure of Risorgimento nationalism.

sources.title: Proletarian nation
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Corradini's proletarian-nation argument, war instead of revolution, opposition to socialism, 'Nationalism is our socialism'.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not an ANI concern; the corporatist state would organise social protection, but nationalists were split and never set a health programme, so this is left neutral.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Nationalists put production and national competitiveness ahead of distribution, so state wage floors imposed on employers are inferred to be disfavoured; unions and state arbitration were to fix wages.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Rocco treated economic activity as subordinate to the national interest and rejected laissez-faire liberal economics, though he favoured private production under state direction.

public-ownership.rationale: The ANI wanted a state-organised industrial economy via cartels and corporate bodies rather than nationalisation; inferred mild opposition to outright public ownership.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Productive owners were counted as part of the proletarian nation, so heavy wealth taxes would cut against its class-collaboration line; inferred from that.

unions-good.rationale: Rocco wanted syndicates turned into state-controlled organs of legal defence, not independent class weapons; unions were acceptable only as subordinated bodies, so adherents are split on the label.

property-fundamental.rationale: Rocco justifies private property by social utility rather than as an inviolable individual right, so it can be overridden for national needs.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The 1914 congress backed state-guided cartels and production policy, and Rocco subordinated economic actors to the nation, implying tighter control of firms.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare is not documented as an ANI theme; nationalists opposed class conflict but not obviously public assistance, and were not aligned on this.

worker-ownership.rationale: Corradini treated owners and entrepreneurs as productive members of the proletarian nation and rejected socialist revolution, so collective worker ownership was not sought.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Rocco puts state security and social needs over individual interests, so counter-terror surveillance is inferred acceptable; anachronistic.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Disciplinary, anti-individualist nationalism would not favour permissive drug policy; inferred, never discussed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; nationalists would restrict anti-national speech but a hate-speech law protecting minorities is not part of the programme.

strong-leader.rationale: Nationalists rejected parliamentary compromise and called for an elitist ruling class and authoritarian state; a leader above gridlock fits that, though the ANI itself was monarchist and elitist rather than leader-cultist.

state-harmful.rationale: Rocco places sovereignty in the juridically organised state and makes it the instrument of the nation, a direct rejection of the claim that the state is harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented position; order and discipline favour state control, but nationalists were not concerned with the question.

empower-police-military.rationale: Militarism was a stated ANI trait, and nationalists wanted strong armed forces for expansion and use of force against socialists.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the anti-individualist, morally disciplinary tone; the sources never discuss it.

decide-locally.rationale: Italian nationalism centres on national unity, and nationalists fought regionalism and federal ideas (Cattaneo, Gioberti) to unify the state.

rehabilitation.rationale: Rocco later codified a severe penal code; punishment and state authority were favoured, but the ANI programme itself is silent.

traditional-family.rationale: Nationalists courted conservative and Catholic opinion and prized traditional institutions, so support is inferred; family was not a core text topic.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from conservative-authoritarian outlook of the movement's mostly right-wing base.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the pro-natal expansionist outlook and conservative Catholic courtship; not documented in sources.

more-religion-public.rationale: Nationalists treated the Church as a traditional institution to build on but were not religious partisans; Rocco praised the Church as a Roman institution while rejecting clericalism.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from nation-first hierarchy and hostility to egalitarian individualism.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's traditional, hierarchical conservatism implies rejection.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural unity and Latin/Roman heritage (Romanita) are at the heart of Italian nationalism as the sources describe.

gradual-change.rationale: Corradini borrowed the revolutionary left's energy and demanded radical national renewal through war; gradualism fits liberal moderates, whom the nationalists despised.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Italy was an emigration country, and nationalists' concern was emigration, not immigration; no documented position.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalists saw the international order as one of plutocratic nations exploiting a proletarian Italy and demanded national struggle, not supranational authority.

free-trade.rationale: The ANI avoided the protectionism dispute to keep members together, but its logic of national economic strength through state-organised industry points against free-trade orthodoxy.

nation-first.rationale: Corradini subordinated everything, including class and individual equality, to the nation's struggle with other nations; national interest over cooperation is central.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Nationalists backed wars of expansion, not human-rights wars; the Mazzinian idea of aiding oppressed peoples belongs to the earlier strand.

open-borders.rationale: Corradini's nation-as-class competition treats nations as bounded rival units; borders were to be extended, not opened.

limit-growth.rationale: Growth and industrialisation were seen as the means for Italy to compete with imperial powers, so limiting them is rejected; environmentalism is anachronistic.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; nationalists would defer to national interest and the question was never framed.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The ANI wanted an industrial state able to compete, and Corradini-style vitalism was pro-modernity; inferred, not stated.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; national power and industrial self-sufficiency imply support.

revolution-justified.rationale: Corradini wanted the left's revolutionary tactics redirected into imperialist war, but the ANI was also monarchist and rejected socialist revolution; adherents divided.

experts-over-public.rationale: Rocco and the ANI called for an elitist ruling class and rejected democracy, so elite expertise over popular opinion fits.

central-planning.rationale: The movement wanted state-organised production and cartels but with private industry, not a fully planned economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not their model; they preferred privately owned production organised through corporate bodies.

land-value-tax.rationale: No documented position on land taxation; neutral.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from conservative base and respect for productive owners; not stated.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred opposition to unconditional entitlement from duty-before-rights outlook.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The ANI declined to take sides publicly, but Italian nationalism's drive for an industrial state able to compete with great powers fits protection; mixed membership kept this at mild support.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The 1914 congress backed production-oriented policy through cartels, and nationalists wanted a state-guided industrial state to compete with empires.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Their model was big industry and cartels for national power; small-property distributism is not documented.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Corradini rejected socialism and anti-national class revolution outright.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Anti-liberal state-centred outlook rejects a market-money position; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: In 1914 the ANI endorsed a corporate state, developed by Rocco, with unions and business bodies replacing parliament to end class conflict.

one-party-rule.rationale: The ANI was an association within a monarchy and only later merged into the Fascist party; its theory favoured an authoritarian elite state but not necessarily a single party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The monarchy was accepted as a traditional institution, and Corradini sat as senator under Victor Emmanuel III, but republicans in the ANI left over it.

democracy-best.rationale: Rocco rejected democracy and parliamentary compromise and called for an elite ruling class.

direct-votes.rationale: Anti-democratic, anti-parliament outlook rejects mass legislating by plebiscite.

workers-councils.rationale: The ANI sought an assembly of unions, businesses and economic organisations under national discipline, not workers' councils as sovereign.

right-to-secede.rationale: National unity was the movement's founding aim, and nationalists fought regionalism and separatist ideas.

natural-rulers.rationale: Rocco argued governing requires a select elite and the masses only have instinctive judgment.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nationalists favoured force against socialists and the Blueshirts were a paramilitary wing; violence in service of the nation was accepted.

war-builds-character.rationale: Corradini stressed martial heroism, discipline and living dangerously, and the ANI welcomed war as national regeneration.

separate-church-state.rationale: Risorgimento nationalism was anti-clerical, but the ANI courted conservative Catholics and accepted the Church as a Roman institution; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Rocco holds the state as sovereign and legal source; religion may support but not rule it.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rocco makes the state the sovereign embodiment of the nation; privatised defense contradicts this.

military-superiority.rationale: Militarism and the aim of acquiring an empire to compete with imperial powers define the ANI.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The article traces Italian identity to Latin descent and unity of one nation; the ANI had a cultural-ethnic view, though not a biological-race doctrine.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Rocco rejects unrestrained class conflict as leading to anarchy; Corradini substituted struggle between nations for class struggle.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Corradini subordinated equality to the nation and discipline; equality of outcomes is rejected.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Anachronistic; nationalism of a settler-colonising state implies opposition.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The ANI championed colonial expansion in Libya and wanted an empire.

civilizational-union.rationale: Mazzini-era visions of Latin unity and Romanita exist, but the ANI was focused on Italy's own national state, not a bloc.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Rocco rejects individualism and makes individuals means of society; selfishness is not a virtue, though productive enterprise was accepted.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Rocco says liberalism puts the individual as end; Fascism and nationalism subordinate him to society, and Mazzini's Duties of Man also puts duty first.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The ANI sources say nothing on nature; adherents are left split on this question, with no stated position to infer from.

limit-population.rationale: Nationalists saw emigration and a large population as a resource for colonial settlement and national power.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The nationalists wanted industrial development as the route to great-power status.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Pro-modernisation and industrial but also tied to institutions; inferred.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic for a 1910s movement; the sources give no basis beyond a general taste for vitalism, so neutral.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; elite-human rule is the stated model.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; state security prioritised over individual privacy.

restore-past-order.rationale: Corradini looked to Roman grandeur but demanded forward radical national renewal, not restoration for its own sake.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The movement was strongly doctrinal about the nation; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Corradini admired the revolutionary left's direct tactics and the ANI's Blueshirts and the later march on Rome were extra-parliamentary.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nationalists accepted ruthlessness and iron discipline as means; not a concern.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Contradicts the industrial and imperial state aims.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Rocco and the ANI wanted organised production through corporations, which presupposes division of labor.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Rocco favoured production over distribution and rejected socialism.

production-for-use.rationale: Rocco's priority on production for the national economy is not the same as non-profit production; private enterprise was kept.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Corradini held that productive owners and entrepreneurs are part of the proletarian nation, rejecting exploitation as the class frame.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Corradini rejected revolutionary socialism and syndicalism.

collective-farming.rationale: Inferred from rejection of socialism and the pro-property social-utility view.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Corradini attacked plutocratic powers but sought to compete with them, not abolish capitalism; he was pro-war himself.

taxation-theft.rationale: Rocco makes the state sovereign over property and individuals, which rejects the claim.

harm-principle.rationale: Rocco subordinates the individual to society's needs, so state power is not limited to preventing harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Rocco explicitly says society, not the individual, is the end; rights do not belong to individuals first.

conscription.rationale: Militarism, discipline and obedience were ANI hallmarks, and the nation's call on citizens is central.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Contrary to Rocco's view that the individual is part of an enduring national society.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is the sovereign embodiment of the nation, not a service firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: Rocco treats the state as providing for society's needs but the sources never frame freedom as material means, so neutral.

media-academia-power.rationale: The sources do not discuss the political power of universities or press; nationalists ran their own press but made no such claim here.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not documented for the ANI; the sources do not discuss racial heredity.

organic-representation.rationale: The 1914 ANI program replaced parliament with an assembly of unions, business groups and economic organisations, the corporate state.

total-state.rationale: Rocco places everything under the state, though his doctrine subordinates rather than eliminates individuals; the ANI itself was less totalising than Fascism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Corradini's radical nationalism demanded national regeneration to end Italy's proletarian status.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Imperial expansion, Libya and an empire were central stated goals.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rocco's state is an impersonal juridical sovereign, not feudal loyalty.

bound-labor.rationale: Modern industrial nationalism, no such position.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism presented its claims as national truth rather than relativism.

universal-morality.rationale: Mazzinian nationalism had universal duties, but the ANI subordinated this to national interest; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Rocco holds that the needs of individuals are identical with those of society as a whole; the national interest was a single good.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Concern with emigrants as colonists of Italian territory suggests sympathy for their link to the homeland; inferred.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not at issue; Italian was already standard.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Authority and discipline within corporations under the state rather than democratic votes.

school-vouchers.rationale: Schooling policy is not discussed in the ANI sources and no stance can be inferred beyond national education, so neutral.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not part of the ANI program as documented, and the movement avoided taking sides on economic disputes.

economic-freedom.rationale: Rocco rejects the liberal doctrine that political freedom rests on individual economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: Nationalists favoured law, discipline and state authority.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Risorgimento tradition holds every nation should have its own state, though the ANI applied it selectively and favoured Italian dominion over others.

force-without-un.rationale: Militarist, expansionist nationalists backed unilateral force, as with Libya in 1911.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Corradini's vitalism and the cult of heroism valued will and sentiment over rationalist inquiry.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Nation-first reasoning implies reserving benefits for citizens; not stated.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Productivism and duty before rights imply work obligations; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: The corporate state aimed to end class conflict by organising employers and workers together.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Romanita and the glory of ancient Rome are central heritage for nationalists.

dominated-front.rationale: Corradini cast Italy as a proletarian nation against plutocratic powers, which would back common cause with other dominated states, though the ANI focused on Italy.

workers-nation.rationale: Corradini explicitly denounced socialist internationalism and held that workers belong to the proletarian nation.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Conservative-authoritarian base; the programme is silent.

ban-interest.rationale: Not documented; the ANI favoured productive private capital.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not part of ANI doctrine at the time; the sources record no such demand.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Rocco treats the state as the organised nation above class.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Cultural unity emphasised, though immigration was not a topic.

proportional-representation.rationale: The ANI rejected parliamentary politics in favour of corporate representation.

national-mission.rationale: Romanita and the Third Rome idea give Italy a civilising mission, though spreading a form of government is not stated.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from conservative base.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nationalists attacked parliamentary politicians and Giolitti as a weak ruling class.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Nationalists defended state force and military; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Rocco's organised state directs the economy and the nation's life.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: The ANI sources define the nation by culture and Latin descent but record no stand on marriage across racial lines.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Corradini's hierarchy of nations and subordination of equality to the nation; Rocco rejects individual egalitarian premises.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Nationalists rejected socialism; question not relevant.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The ANI promoted Italian settler colonisation of Libya as national policy.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Unified national law fits the unitary state; not documented.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious conversion is not discussed in the sources; the ANI was only loosely tied to the Church, so neutral.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religious instruction was not a defining ANI issue; split between anti-clerical and Catholic currents.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Not applicable to a non-socialist ideology.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Rocco locates sovereignty in the organised state, not in the people.

trade-surplus.rationale: Economic nationalism favours strong national industry and exports; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: The sources record no ANI demand to expel minorities; irredentist claims concerned annexing territory, so no position is stated.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Imperialist war and conquest are explicit aims.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Corradini treated struggle between nations as the engine of history and demanded national competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Nationalists favoured state defence against subversive socialists; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Rocco and the ANI wanted authority concentrated in the state, and rejected parliamentary compromise.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist concept; Corradini borrowed revolutionary discipline but for nation, not class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Nationalism claimed the proletarian nation in aggregate rather than the poor as a class.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing tenure is outside the ANI's concerns in the sources, and nothing can be inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Rocco classes strikes and lockouts as disorder, to be replaced by state adjudication.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Nationalists saw emigration as caused by lack of colonies, not overpopulation as such.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Cultural unity is a nationalist premise, though ethnic diversity within Italy was not the focus.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Contrary to an elite ruling class.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authoritarian nationalists favoured force against socialists and state supremacy.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls are not mentioned in the sources; a state-guided economy might allow them in wartime but adherents are not documented either way.

party-controls-media.rationale: The ANI had its own press (L'Idea Nazionale) but media control is not a documented demand.

party-commands-army.rationale: Monarchist nationalists treated the army as a national, monarchical institution.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Discipline and obedience were valued; party structures not documented.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Nationalists opposed supranational authority in favour of national struggle.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The monarchist ANI accepted the king as head of state and commander.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance was not a nationalist concern; the ANI valued the Church as a Roman institution without taking a view on its internal structure.

clerical-rule.rationale: Rocco makes the state sovereign, and Risorgimento nationalism was anti-clerical.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Corradini condemned socialist anti-patriotism and anti-militarism.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not documented, though a disciplinary state might.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Rocco's authoritarian state would not care about term limits, but the ANI was monarchist and the sources do not discuss presidents.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Nationalists first favoured the Triple Alliance and then the Entente; they chose alliances as it served expansion.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: No tie to doctrine; contrary to socialism rejection.

people-in-arms.rationale: Militarist and mass-mobilising but a professional army was the norm.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Nationalists wanted industrialisation but also valued southern peasants as colonists; split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Irredentism, claiming Austrian-held Italian-populated lands, is the ANI's founding cause.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The sources give no stance on university-educated people; nationalist intellectuals like Corradini were themselves educated, so neutral.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Romanita and Latin superiority and imperial mission mean the ANI ranked civilisations.

death-penalty.rationale: Authoritarian outlook; Rocco later oversaw a harsher criminal code.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The sources do not touch evolution or school science; Catholic courtship cuts one way and modernising vitalism the other, so neutral.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Italian identity as a Latin-descended nation implies descent-based membership; also tied to emigrants.

minority-language-support.rationale: Cultural unity and irredentism imply assimilation, but they were not prominent on this.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Rocco puts the state first, so general law over exemptions; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Corradini stressed discipline, obedience and the subordination of individualism.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Sovereign debt of poor countries is not addressed; Italy itself was resented as dependent on richer powers but no debt policy is documented.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Corradini argued Italy's political unity was undermined by economic dependence on richer powers.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Authoritarian industrial state to compete with empires fits.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nation-first and anti-plutocratic stance rejects a duty of the wealthy to the world's poor.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Monarchist and elitist, against mass electoral politics.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The state subordinated economy to national interest.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Irredentist claims on historic lands, and the myth of the mutilated victory, fit.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Rocco says property is a problem of social utility.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The Soviet Union post-dates the ANI's founding, and the sources record no nationalist theory of it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk policy is anachronistic for the ANI, and no position can be inferred from its stated principles.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance membership was accepted when useful (Triple Alliance, Entente).

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Irredentists wanted Austrian-held lands annexed by Italy, and nationalists viewed annexations favouring Italian claims as legitimate; consent of populations was not the test.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Mazzinian anti-clericalism versus the ANI's courting of Catholics; split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The monarchy as above-party national symbol was accepted by the ANI.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Unity of Italy was a core goal.

region-keeps-system.rationale: A unitary national state was favoured.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Not claimed; the monarchy was a traditional institution only.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Tax structure is not discussed in the sources, and productive owners being part of the nation does not settle flat versus progressive rates.

character-from-environment.rationale: Vitalism and national spirit stress will and heritage; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The sovereign state is juridically organised, in Rocco, not arbitrary.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is anachronistic; territorial expansion was central but on Earth, so this is left neutral.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Monarchy plus corporate assembly is mixed, but this is not a stated doctrine.

leader-cult.rationale: ANI itself did not develop a cult; later fascism did; adherents split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law is not covered in the sources and a nationalist stance cannot be inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: Not addressed; Italian exiles from claimed lands would be a nationalist concern; inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Irredentism claims territories because Italians live there.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not addressed; state is secular sovereign.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Latin unity talk existed in the Risorgimento but the ANI was Italy-focused.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Unitary nationalism implies assimilation not autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Not addressed for Jews; for Italians the ANI favoured emigrants becoming colonists in Italian territory.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Corradini rejected Marxist materialism and placed nation and will first.

no-bailouts.rationale: State rescue of firms is not discussed, and a state-guided industrial economy could go either way, so neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Not addressed; rejects both liberal limits and mass rule.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The aim of an industrial state with an empire to compete suggests an autarkic bloc, though not stated as such.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Binding international standards would be a supranational constraint, which the nationalists disliked, though they never discussed trade agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: Duty, sacrifice and discipline are core virtues.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Not a stated doctrine though the later Blueshirts operated.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Romanita and national heritage taught centrally.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The ANI justified Libya and empire as bringing Italians settlement and Roman civilisation; adherents saw advanced rule as right.

patriotic-education.rationale: Cultural unity and national pride were central.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preferences in admissions are an anachronistic issue the ANI never faced, and nothing can be inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary design is not mentioned in the sources, so no position is stated.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Corradini sought to harness capitalist production for the nation, not collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Nationalists aimed to revive Roman glory and influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Wanted an industrial competitive economy, not delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: This Marxist thesis about workers in rich countries is not addressed; Corradini treated Italy as proletarian as a whole, not split by labor.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Rocco rejects individual rights as limits on the organised state.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Nationalists were colonisers, but they also resented treaties like London's partial delivery, a 'mutilated victory'; inferred mixed, leaning against voiding treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: The ANI accepted monarchy as a traditional institution and rejected mass democracy; republicans left the association over it.

minority-veto.rationale: Rocco puts sovereignty in the organised state and rejects individual consent as foundation.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Statist nationalism stresses obedience and discipline; resistance rights are not part of it.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The ANI wanted to replace parliament with an assembly of economic bodies and rejected parliamentary compromise.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Class collaboration and duty of the productive classes to the nation imply a duty of owners; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Corradini demanded active heroic engagement and sacrifice for the nation.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: The ANI sources contain no media-critique theory, and nationalists themselves used the press for mobilisation, so neutral.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian idea not addressed in the nationalist sources, so neutral.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Corradini argued Italy was a proletarian nation exploited by plutocratic powers and international capitalism, a close analogue.

native-born-offices.rationale: Nation-first stance implies it; not documented.

party-own-road.rationale: Not applicable to a nationalist movement.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Economic nationalism favours national self-strengthening, inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The movement's irredentism demanded Trento, Trieste and other lands from Austria and later Dalmatia.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: ANI's colonial expansion in Libya aimed to establish Italian settlers.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Nationalists merged into the Fascist party in 1923 and are tied to Fascism.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Nationalists fought socialists and allied with Fascism; equating them would not fit, though they were not all totalitarian.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: The American Civil War lies outside the ANI's concerns and the sources say nothing on it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Heritage and Roman glory prized; inferred.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; the traditionalist base is unlikely to oppose it but the program is silent, so neutral.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence is not addressed in the sources, and a nationalist stance cannot be inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Nationalists stressed distinct national character over imported liberal models; mild inference.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Militarism and the prestige of the army in national life were stated traits.

office-by-exam.rationale: The sources do not cover civil-service selection; an elitist ruling class might favour merit but nothing is documented.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Economic nationalism favours national control of industry; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: State organises social needs in the corporate model; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Property is justified by social utility but remains private; inferred.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament was to be replaced or sidelined.

single-official-language.rationale: Cultural unity under a national language fits unitary nationalism; minority languages were not a core issue.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Disparate-impact doctrine is anachronistic, but the movement's rejection of egalitarian individualism makes agreement very unlikely.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Heroic, disciplinary vitalism disdained bourgeois comfort; inferred from Corradini's 'living dangerously'.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Expansionist nationalism and irredentism implies support; inferred.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The ANI backed alliances of convenience and imperial expansion but did not discuss great-power control over allies, so neutral.

corporate-influence.rationale: The ANI wanted business bodies to join in running the state, but also attacked plutocrats; split.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population as national strength and emigration worries imply support; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on home purchases are not discussed in the sources and nationalism's focus was on the nation, not localities.

job-guarantee.rationale: Employment guarantees are not part of the documented ANI program, though the corporate state was meant to organise production, so neutral.

democratic-peace.rationale: ANI nationalists rejected democracy and valued war.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Rocco makes obedience to the state a duty of members of society.

non-intervention.rationale: Expansionist nationalists claimed the right to intervene and conquer, e.g. Libya.

industrial-unions.rationale: Rocco wanted syndicates under state control, whichever form they took.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The ANI had anti-masonic hostility in the sources but not a documented minority conspiracy.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The sources record no stance on transparency, and an authoritarian elite state would not prioritise it, so it is left neutral.

informal-organisation.rationale: Prefers discipline and organised state structures.

religious-nation.rationale: Nationalism defined the nation by Latin culture and descent, with the Church a supporting institution, not the nation's definition.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Corradini condemned Italy's subordination to plutocratic powers.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Unitary nationalism opposed regional egoism; north-south divide challenges the unity it wants.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The question presumes common ownership of production, which the ANI rejected, but personal belongings are not at issue for it.

defeat-communism.rationale: Corradini rejected revolutionary socialism and the ANI used force against socialists.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Service delivery models are not covered; the ANI wanted state-organised but privately owned production, so no clear stance.

religion-illusion.rationale: Rocco praises the Church as a surviving Roman institution.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Corradini saw productive entrepreneurs as part of the nation and wanted industrial development.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed; nationalists resented the London settlement; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Colonisation by Italian settlers was a key aim.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The corporate state was a third way between liberal capitalism and socialism, as the sources frame it.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Irredentism relied on Roman and historical Italian ties to lands.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not addressed; ANI predates the Holocaust and the sources do not cover it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The sources record no ANI stance on this; Rocco later drafted a harsh penal code but this was not addressed.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Nationalists favoured force to control socialists and rejected democratic pluralism.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The state is sovereign; not addressed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The ANI framed colonies as outlets and advantage for proletarian Italy.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A question about Islamic doctrine on invasion that Italian nationalism did not address, though it itself backed invading Libya.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: A question on Islamic rulers that Italian nationalism never addressed, so the answer is a low-confidence rejection based on its secular state sovereignty.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Rejects democratic participation in favour of elite rule.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Corradini borrowed socialist language for nationalism and ANI members held varied forms, rejecting the framework.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed; Libya's war was colonial, not religious per the sources.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Rocco locates sovereignty in the state, not God; Mazzini's God and people are another strand.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress in state institutions is not in the sources; Catholic accommodation and state supremacy pull opposite ways.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace harassment law is anachronistic and absent from the sources, so no position is stated.

social-market-economy.rationale: Not their formula; they wanted a state-guided corporatist economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Militarism is a stated ANI trait.

rich-first.rationale: Unequal development was accepted for building national industry; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The ANI first backed the Triple Alliance and then pushed entry into the war on the Entente side, opposing neutralists.

property-franchise.rationale: ANI was elitist but its base was wealthy; no stated franchise demand.

reification.rationale: Marxist concept; not part of tradition.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: A socialist critique that Corradini rejected.

racial-franchise.rationale: Not documented for the ANI; nation defined culturally.

open-government-data.rationale: Open data portals are anachronistic and the ANI's elite model gives no basis for an answer, so neutral.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Marriage between religions is not addressed; the ANI defined the nation by culture and descent, not faith, so mild disagreement is inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The sources record no ANI boycott campaign against a minority; the movement's anti-masonic stance was political, so mild rejection is inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not discussed, and nationalist support for the Church as a Roman institution gives no view on doctrine.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not a nationalist concern; productive owners valued.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Rocco credits the Church and the ANI courted Catholics.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Unitary nationalism rejects consociational division; inferred.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The sources do not compare charity with state aid, and the corporate state was meant to organise social needs, so neutral.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred: the ANI wanted a strong elitist state led by an experienced ruling class and disliked parliamentary rotation, so limiting tenure cuts against its view of authority.

vote-delegation.rationale: Rocco and the ANI rejected individual popular sovereignty and mass democracy in favour of the state above individuals, so delegable citizen voting runs against a core principle.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred: the movement prized national expansion, war and greatness over humanity-wide concerns, and it predates the idea of extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the ANI came to value the Catholic Church as a national institution and held traditional social hierarchies, so women's ordination was not an aim.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred: the ANI's hierarchical, corporatist view of society and family fits male headship, as in contemporary Italian family law.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: the ANI made citizenship and national belonging exclusive and the nation was above individuals.

rent-control.rationale: Corporatism regulated class relations by the state but housing policy was not addressed; split.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from its stress on national property and production.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from its militarism and discipline of youth for national service; not stated in sources opened.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its drive for great-power strength and military prestige.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Sovereignty and national independence from richer powers were central; inferred for foreign bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic; the colonial wars it championed involved mass violence the movement would not condemn.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The proletarian-nation idea and corporatism favoured rewarding producers over rentiers and plutocrats; inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The movement glorified war and conquest, so a duty never to kill contradicts its doctrine.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Italian nationalism claims Latin and Roman continuity as the foundation of the nation.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its traditional, hierarchical and organic view of society.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its collectivist and traditional view of society.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The cult of the fallen and of irredentist and colonial war dead was central to nationalist rhetoric.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Rocco treated the state as an ethical and spiritual entity but did not frame politics as good against evil; split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Nationalists sought to gather Italians in the nation and its colonies rather than leave a diaspora as a cultural periphery.

culture-before-state.rationale: Rocco's doctrine places the state first; the nation is realised through the state.

god-not-male.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from its traditionalism and its alliance with the monarchy and Church.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred: the corporatist state placed the economy under national direction.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Irredentism aimed to bring Italian-inhabited lands (Trentino, Trieste, Dalmatia) into one Italian state.

independent-unions.rationale: Corradini and Rocco wanted class organisations subordinated to the nation, with syndicates under state control.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Rocco's corporatism rejected worker power as socialist class struggle and put the state above classes.

local-essentials-public.rationale: A state-directed corporatist order favours public control of strategic services; inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Rocco favoured an elitist, anti-parliamentary state; inferred that a non-elected chamber of the elite is acceptable.

municipal-property.rationale: The nationalists opposed both socialist ownership and local autonomy; ownership is held under national direction; inferred.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Rocco's state is centralised and sovereign, leaving no room for local assemblies.

family-wage.rationale: Corporatist nationalism was pro-natalist and wanted wages to sustain the national family; inferred.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; inferred indifference.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; inferred indifference.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The state sovereign over all economic life would not accept untraceable payments; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: The authoritarian state demanding discipline would not accept anonymity; inferred.

person-over-state.rationale: Rocco states the individual is subordinate to the state, which is the end and the individual the means.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Rocco contrasted nationalism's spiritual values with materialist socialism; low confidence as the doctrine is not about human nature.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The unitary, sovereign state forbids rival authorities; regional powers can only be granted and withdrawn.

gm-crops.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; inferred indifference.

dense-cities.rationale: Not an issue for the movement; inferred indifference.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The movement spoke of the Italian nation and a 'proletarian nation', not of racial groups; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in Roman and Latin heritage is central to the movement; the sources frame it as national, so low confidence for race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The movement demanded colonial and irredentist expansion and glorified war.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Irredentism claimed Italian-speaking lands such as Trentino and Trieste across state borders, resting on shared Italian language and heritage.

communal-electorates.rationale: Rocco's state stands above groups and demands one sovereign national authority, so separate religious electorates are inferred to be rejected.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Corradini cast Italy as a proletarian nation held back by plutocratic powers; a partition plot is inferred as a natural extension, not stated.

free-public-college.rationale: Inferred from the elitist, anti-egalitarian outlook of the ANI; it never set an education-funding policy.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement never addressed pollution and nothing in its principles favours or opposes taxes on it.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist view of the nation as a lasting community over generations; no statement on the environment.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred from the movement's martial, hierarchical values, which gave no weight to a distinct women's outlook.

arms-reduction.rationale: The ANI was militarist and sought expansion through war, so cutting armaments to a minimum runs against its core.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the great-power, elitist view of foreign policy as a state matter; open diplomacy was not discussed.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from the corporatist state directing the economy in the national interest against plutocratic powers.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from Rocco's doctrine that the state alone holds sovereign force; the ANI's own Blueshirt squads are the exception.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The ANI was militarist and valued war as national regeneration, so refusal of orders is the opposite of its creed.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Rocco's corporatism had state-recognised syndicates make collective labour contracts, though under state control rather than free bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: nationalists put production above distribution, and the corporate state would not top up wages through taxes.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from Rocco's view that the sovereign state is above individual rules and should not be legally bound.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Corradini's 'proletarian nation' argued poor nations were exploited by plutocratic powers and should change the world order, by war.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Rocco sought to strengthen and reshape the state from within as the supreme authority, not to smash it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Rocco's corporate state imposes a single national economic order and rejects laissez-faire pluralism.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: nature as capital is a liberal-economic idea alien to the doctrine; not discussed.

sacred-nation.rationale: Rocco presents the nation as a moral, enduring community that transcends individuals and gives them their meaning.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: sacrifice and discipline were preached over individual relief; student debt is anachronistic.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Nationalists denied class and regional exploitation inside the nation, blaming foreign plutocracies instead.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Rocco rejects liberal individual rights and subordinates the person to the state, so dignity is not grounded in a fixed human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: an authoritarian state would control the press rather than fund media free of government control.

missingStatements.text: A nation that is poor and exploited by richer powers should seek expansion and war rather than internal class revolution.
missingStatements.rationale: Corradini's 'proletarian nation' replaced class revolution with imperialist war and conquest.
missingStatements.declined: Corradini's proletarian-nation doctrine is specific to this ideology; no other ideology would meaningfully take a side.

missingStatements.text: Emigration from a country should be replaced by settlement of its own colonies.
missingStatements.rationale: Nationalists argued colonial expansion would let Italian emigrants settle Italian territory instead of labouring abroad.
missingStatements.declined: Specific to Italian colonial emigration debates; colonies-serve-metropole and economic bloc statements cover the wider theme.

notes: The Mazzinian and Cavourian Risorgimento strands would answer differently: republican or liberal, anti-clerical, pro-democracy (Mazzini) and wary of conquest. Post-1945 nationalism (MSI, Alleanza Nazionale, Lega, Brothers of Italy) is not covered. The ANI was internally mixed (authoritarian, democratic and revolutionary currents), so stated positions follow the program of 1910-1914 and Rocco's doctrine.
